strings.name: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner
strings.role: Former president and vice president of Argentina; president of the Justicialist Party
strings.summary: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner is a prominent figure in Argentine Peronism, serving as president in 2007–2015 and vice president in 2019–2023. Her administration expanded social protection and state economic participation. Since her roadworks conviction became final in 2025, she has served her sentence under house arrest while remaining involved in party affairs.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 18 November 2026, with recent activity based on the reported balcony appearance on the 17th. The final roadworks judgment is distinguished from unresolved charges in other cases. Supporters’ hopes for a 2027 candidacy do not mean her public-office ban has been lifted.
strings.influence.rationale: As a former Argentine president and vice president, she has long influenced the Peronist movement and the country’s economic, social and foreign policies.
strings.facts.f1.label: Legal education
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied at the National University of La Plata. A university statement cited in fact-checking coverage confirms completion of her law studies in October 1979 and issuance of her law degree on 10 December. This should not be described as a doctorate.
strings.facts.f2.label: Political career
strings.facts.f2.value: Entered the Santa Cruz provincial legislature in 1989, later serving as a national deputy, senator, president and vice president. The Justicialist Party presidency is a party office, distinct from the national presidency.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Social protection and state economic participation
strings.highlights.h1.text: Her presidency established the AUH child allowance and promoted state control of YPF, reflecting an emphasis on social protection and state involvement in the economy. Policy objectives, legislative measures and actual economic effects require separate assessment.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Judicial findings and her response
strings.highlights.h2.text: In the roadworks case, she was convicted of fraudulent administration to the detriment of the public administration, receiving six years’ imprisonment and a lifetime public-office ban. She was acquitted of unlawful association in that case. She denies wrongdoing and alleges political persecution; court findings and her position are distinguished.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Greets supporters at a gathering
strings.timeline.t1.text: Página/12 reported that she greeted supporters from her balcony while under house arrest. This entry relies on the visible headline and standfirst; no live video was watched, and the appearance does not imply release.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Participates in a separate trial hearing
strings.timeline.t2.text: According to El País the following day, she remotely attended the opening of the combined Hotesur and Los Sauces trial. Alleged money laundering and other conduct in this case must be distinguished from the final roadworks conviction; charges are not convictions.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Roadworks conviction becomes final
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Supreme Court rejected the appeal, making the 2022 sentence of six years and lifetime public-office ban final. House arrest is a way of serving the sentence; a September 2026 review maintained that arrangement.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Takes over national Justicialist Party leadership
strings.timeline.t4.text: Succeeded Alberto Fernández as president of the Justicialist Party’s National Council. November 2026 reporting still identifies her as party president; this is leadership of a party organisation.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes vice president of Argentina
strings.timeline.t5.text: Joined President Alberto Fernández as his governing partner, serving as vice president until 10 December 2023. This office is distinct from her earlier presidential terms.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Congress passes law to expropriate control of YPF
strings.timeline.t6.text: Law 26741 designated a 51% stake in YPF, held by Repsol, for expropriation and allocation between the national state and oil-producing provinces. It did not expropriate the entire company or oil industry. The law was published on 7 May.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Signs child-allowance decree
strings.timeline.t7.text: Decree 1602/2009 created the non-contributory AUH child allowance for eligible children in unemployed or informal-sector households. It was published on the 30th. The name ‘universal’ does not mean unconditional payments to everyone.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Begins first presidential term
strings.timeline.t8.text: Succeeded Néstor Kirchner as president and began a second term in 2011. The presidential historical archive dates the end of her second term to 9 December 2015.
